covers: The vector slots at the top of the 6809's memory; 0xFFF0 is reserved and no code reads it

entries.name: SWI3
entries.behaviour: SWI3 sets the effective address to this vector, runs SOFTWARE_INTERRUPT, which sets the E flag and pushes every register on S, and does not change the I and F flags. INTERRUPT_VECTOR then reads the new PC, high byte from the vector and low byte from the next.

entries.name: SWI2
entries.behaviour: SWI2 sets the effective address to this vector, runs SOFTWARE_INTERRUPT, which sets the E flag and pushes every register on S, and does not change the I and F flags. INTERRUPT_VECTOR then reads the new PC, high byte from the vector and low byte from the next.

entries.name: FIRQ
entries.description: Where a fast interrupt request goes.
entries.behaviour: Taken before an instruction when the F flag is clear and the FIRQ line is asserted. It clears E and pushes the partial state (firq_saves_entire_state is false), sets I and F, and the standard interrupt callback runs. INTERRUPT_VECTOR then reads the new PC, high byte from the vector and low byte from the next.

entries.name: IRQ
entries.behaviour: Taken before an instruction when the I flag is clear and the IRQ line is asserted, after NMI and FIRQ. It sets E, pushes every register, sets I and not F, and the standard interrupt callback runs. INTERRUPT_VECTOR then reads the new PC, high byte from the vector and low byte from the next.

entries.name: SWI
entries.behaviour: SWI sets E, pushes every register and sets I and F, so it inhibits IRQ and FIRQ, unlike SWI2 and SWI3. INTERRUPT_VECTOR then reads the new PC, high byte from the vector and low byte from the next.

entries.name: NMI
entries.behaviour: Taken before an instruction while m_nmi_asserted is set, ahead of FIRQ and IRQ. It clears that flag, sets E, pushes every register, sets I and F, and the standard interrupt callback runs. INTERRUPT_VECTOR then reads the new PC, high byte from the vector and low byte from the next.

entries.name: reset
entries.description: Where the cpu starts after a reset.
entries.behaviour: device_reset clears the direct page register, sets the I and F flags, points the effective address at this vector (VECTOR_RESET_FFFE) and resets the sub-instruction state.
